t: In front of you is the London and North Western Railway War Memorial, outside Euston station. It remembers the company's employees who were killed in the First World War. About 37,000 of them left to fight, around a third of the workforce, and more than 3,000 did not come back. The memorial was designed by Reginald Wynn Owen, the railway's own architect. It cost twelve and a half thousand pounds. The employees gave four thousand of that, and the company paid the rest.
